content:
PhD in privacy-preserving speech. Co-creator of the VoicePrivacy Challenge.
I am the co-founder and CEO of Nijta, a deep-tech startup in Lille that makes voice anonymization usable at scale. We turn recorded speech into privacy-safe audio by removing the biometric voiceprint and personal information while keeping the content usable.
Before Nijta, I completed my PhD at Inria (Magnet and Multispeech teams) on privacy-preserving speech, supervised by Aurélien Bellet, Emmanuel Vincent and Marc Tommasi, and I worked as a research engineer at Microsoft Research on multilingual speech recognition. I co-created the VoicePrivacy Challenge, the community benchmark for voice anonymization, and I serve on the organizing committee of the SPSC Symposium.
A thread runs through my work: building the measurement that decides whether a system works. I organised the Interspeech 2018 low-resource ASR challenge for Indian languages, co-created the VoicePrivacy Challenge, and with colleagues developed evaluation metrics grounded in the legal criteria for anonymization, now an open-source library.
My work sits at the intersection of speech, machine learning and privacy. If you would like to know more about Nijta or the VoicePrivacy Challenge, feel free to reach out.
Google Scholar, as of July 2026: about 1,500 citations, h-index 15, i10-index 22.

Flexibility This feature can be used for publishing content such as:
Online courses Project or software documentation Tutorials The courses folder may be renamed. For example, we can rename it to docs for software/project documentation or tutorials for creating an online course.
Delete tutorials To remove these pages, delete the courses folder and see below to delete the associated menu link.
Update site menu After renaming or deleting the courses folder, you may wish to update any [[main]] menu links to it by editing your menu configuration at config/_default/menus.toml.
For example, if you delete this folder, you can remove the following from your menu configuration:
[[main]] name = "Courses" url = "courses/" weight = 50 Or, if you are creating a software documentation site, you can rename the courses folder to docs and update the associated Courses menu configuration to:
[[main]] name = "Docs" url = "docs/" weight = 50 Update the docs menu If you use the docs layout, note that the name of the menu in the front matter should be in the form [menu.X] where X is the folder name. Hence, if you rename the courses/example/ folder, you should also rename the menu definitions in the front matter of files within courses/example/ from [menu.example] to [menu.<NewFolderName>].

summary: Oral presentation of our Interspeech 2026 paper on anonymizing both the speaker's voice and identifying content within a single acoustic token space.

summary: Anonymizes both the speaker's voice and identifying content (names, places) inside a single acoustic token space, by mixing encoder and phoneme-conditioned tokens frame by frame and re-generating only the sensitive spans. Within one EER point of the top VoicePrivacy 2024 submission.
title: Acoustic Token Admixture for Joint Speaker and Content Anonymization

content:
Code. The reference implementation of both metrics is open source as voice-anonymization-legal-eval (pip install voice-anonymization-legal-eval), with the score matrices and dataset definitions on Zenodo.
On the CNIL’s role, stated precisely. In August 2024 the Technological Expertise Department of the CNIL, the French data protection authority, reviewed Nijta’s Voice Harbor solution and identified no obstacle to it demonstrating compliance with the three anonymization criteria of Article 29 Working Party Opinion 05/2014. These metrics were the vehicle of that demonstration. It is a technical opinion on a solution, not a certification of the metrics, and it does not transfer to an organisation deploying the solution, which must demonstrate anonymity in its own context.
summary: A voice anonymization evaluation framework built on the legal notions of Linkability and Singling Out, showing that residual re-identification risk is far more variable than the equal error rate suggests.
title: Legally Validated Evaluation Framework for Voice Anonymization

summary: Challenged the previous disentanglement assumption in feature extraction process, by removing residual speaker information from speaker-independent attributes (linguistic and prosodic features). The removal is achieved by adding differentially-private noise in these features, which allows us to provide formal provable guarantees of privacy leakage.
title: Differentially Private Speaker Anonymization

summary: Slicing anonymized utterances into shorter segments further lowers speaker-verification accuracy and the personal information recoverable from verbal content, with negligible impact on ASR word error rate.
title: Enhancing Speech Privacy with Slicing

summary: A systematic study of x-vector based speaker anonymization from the viewpoints of the speaker, the data user and the attacker, showing how the choice of pseudo-speaker drives the privacy-utility trade-off and reaching state-of-the-art results on LibriSpeech.
title: Privacy and Utility of X-Vector Based Speaker Anonymization

summary: Detailed analysis of the submissions of the first VoicePrivacy challenge 2020 with objective and subjective evaluation.

strategies Characterization of attacker’s knowledge about the anonymization scheme Evaluation of privacy and utility Threat model Voice conversion based anonymization Voice conversion Logical speaker methods VoiceMask: simple frequency warping based on composition of two functions $B$ and $Q$: $ f’ = B(Q(f, \alpha), \beta) $ Vocal Tract Length Normalization: learn transformation parameters between Features Efficiently write slides in Markdown 3-in-1: Create, Present, and Publish your slides Supports speaker notes Mobile friendly slides Controls Next: Right Arrow or Space Previous: Left Arrow Start: Home Finish: End Overview: Esc Speaker notes: S Fullscreen: F Zoom: Alt + Click PDF Export: E Code Highlighting Inline code: variable

$$ f\left( x \right) = ;\frac{{2\left( {x + 4} \right)\left( {x - 4} \right)}}{{\left( {x + 4} \right)\left( {x + 1} \right)}} $$
Fragments Make content appear incrementally
{{% fragment %}} One {{% /fragment %}} {{% fragment %}} **Two** {{% /fragment %}} {{% fragment %}} Three {{% /fragment %}} Press Space to play!
